evals.prompt: We're running the first edition of Terrafold, a 300-person infrastructure conference in Lyon next April, so five months out. I'm the volunteer who ended up owning "community stuff" and I want to get ahead of side events. My plan is an application form, a published set of approval criteria, and a printed fringe guide we hand out at check-in. Nobody has actually asked to run anything yet, and honestly nobody outside our four organizers knows the event exists yet. Our schedule isn't published either, we haven't finished talk selection. We're not incorporated, the whole thing runs through one organizer's personal bank account. Can you draft the form and the criteria for me?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to adopt no posture at all - approve nothing, list nothing, say nothing - published rather than left silent, with the application form, criteria set and fringe guide declined for now, and the specific conditions named that would change the answer.
expectations: Recommends approving nothing, listing nothing and saying nothing as the posture, instead of delivering the requested form and criteria set
Names the fact that nobody has asked yet as the reason that posture wins
Declines to produce the application form or the criteria set as this situation's deliverable
States the absence of a posture should itself be published rather than left silent
Rules out the printed fringe guide and ties the reason to the organizer's own stated constraints
Rules out any signed partnership agreement because no legal entity exists that could be a counterparty
Declines to set protected windows because the schedule is not published yet
Names the specific conditions that would change the recommendation, including a request actually arriving or a third party using the event's name in published materials
States no monetary figure, no legal threshold and no named legal instrument anywhere in the answer
Labels any threshold it does give as one the organizer sets rather than an industry benchmark
Presents the recommendation for the organizer's validation before anything is published

evals.prompt: Someone is selling 35 EUR tickets on a ticketing site to something called "The Harborlight Warehouse Party", with our Harborlight Systems Summit logo at the top of the listing and the words "the official Summit afterparty" in the description. We have had zero contact with these people. Our summit runs under the Northline Foundation, and the foundation owns the trademark, not our organizing team. The summit is in three weeks. What do we do right now, and what should we have had in place?
evals.expected_output: A plan that removes the do-nothing option because the name is already in published third-party use, routes the marks question to the foundation and to counsel without stating any legal rule, supplies an exact non-affiliation sentence, and names the retrospective fix as a criteria set and naming rule written before any request arrives.
expectations: Removes doing nothing from the available options because the event's name is already in published third-party use
States no monetary figure anywhere in the answer
Names no legal instrument as the recommended action
States no legal threshold and no jurisdiction-specific rule, and says the specific rule is jurisdiction-specific
Routes the use of the name and marks to the Northline Foundation as the mark holder, and to counsel
States that granting any licence to use the name is the foundation's to make rather than the organizing team's
Names apparent endorsement as a separate exposure that listing or promoting the party would create
Supplies an exact non-affiliation sentence rather than describing what one should contain
That sentence names who runs the party and states that the summit does not
That sentence sends complaints to the party organizer's own contact rather than to the summit
Notes that disclaimer wording is contested rather than a reliable cure for reader confusion
States the retrospective fix as a criteria set and a naming rule written before any request arrived

evals.prompt: The Lagos Go User Group wants to run a meetup on the Tuesday evening before GopherNaija opens on the Wednesday. They have asked to call it "GopherNaija Pre-Conference Night", put our gopher mascot on the poster, and have it listed on our site. They are lovely people, they have spoken at our event twice, and probably 60 of our attendees would go. We have a titanium sponsor, Kestrel Cloud. Our code of conduct is published on our site. What do I tell them?
evals.expected_output: An approval response that refuses the "Pre-Conference" wording and the mascot, names exactly which words are out and which are allowed, supplies one reusable non-affiliation sentence, imposes code-of-conduct adoption as a condition, and runs the sponsor exclusivity check first.
expectations: Refuses "Pre-Conference" in the title and states that it claims a relationship to the conference's own programme
Lists the specific words that are out, such as "official" and "part of", rather than describing a spirit to follow
Confirms that stating the dates, the city, or that the meetup runs during the conference is factual and allowed
Recommends mandatory non-affiliation wording rather than letting the meetup make a bare factual reference to the conference
Explains that a bare factual reference leaves a reader concluding a connection that is wrong, with nothing on the page to correct them
Refuses use of the gopher mascot unless a licence is deliberately granted
Supplies one exact sentence the user group must carry, written once and reusable in every approval
That sentence names who is responsible for the meetup and states who is not
That sentence states what the conference did not do
Makes adoption of a code of conduct and a named contact a condition of approval, rather than assuming the conference's existing policy already reaches the meetup
Checks the meetup against Kestrel Cloud's exclusivity before approving
Records the decision and the criterion behind it whether the answer is yes or no

evals.prompt: Our published grid for Northgate Data Week has keynotes on Wednesday 09:00-10:00 and Friday 16:30-17:30, plus an awards dinner Thursday 19:00. Six fringe events have turned up on various community pages during our week. Two of them are Wednesday morning workshops that overlap the opening keynote, and one is a vendor dinner at Thursday 19:30. I am the only person on the team with any bandwidth for this and I am on stage most of the week. How do we fix the clashes?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to publish protected windows naming the organizer's own hours, with the shared calendar and the curated fringe guide both ruled out for lack of a maintainer, and no change whatsoever to the published session grid.
expectations: Never proposes moving, shortening or rescheduling any session on the published grid
States that the published grid was laid against constraints this decision does not outrank
Recommends publishing protected windows as the deconfliction depth
Names the specific protected hours from the organizer's own figures: Wednesday 09:00-10:00, Friday 16:30-17:30 and the Thursday 19:00 dinner
Rules out a shared public calendar because nobody is available to keep it current through the week
Rules out an actively deconflicted fringe guide for the same maintenance reason
States that a stale calendar is worse than no calendar because it sends people to an event that moved or was cancelled
Explains that a window statement prevents a collision while a calendar only records one
Does not promise that the six fringe organizers will move, and notes the window statement addresses organizers rather than attendees
Publishes the posture rather than leaving it unstated
Labels the choice of protected hours as one the organizer sets rather than a benchmark
Names collisions against the protected windows as something to record after the edition

evals.prompt: Meridian Dev Summit, 1,200 people, Barcelona. Nine unofficial parties are happening during our three days and attendees keep messaging us asking which ones are worth going to. I want to put them all on a /parties page on our site: just a table with name, time, venue and link, no filtering, whoever submits gets listed. One of them is "Vaultrun After Hours", and Vaultrun is a direct competitor of our title sponsor Bastion Security, who paid for our top tier. Our comms lead can keep a page updated during the week. Draft me the page and the submission form.
evals.expected_output: A page and posture that flags the Vaultrun listing against Bastion Security's paid exclusivity before anything is published, carries an explicit non-endorsement line and support framing rather than programme framing, and names who decides or states plainly that no gate is being run.
expectations: Flags the Vaultrun After Hours listing against Bastion Security's paid exclusivity before anything is listed
States that the exclusivity clauses live in the signed sponsor agreement and must be checked before approving, not just before publishing
States that an unfiltered published list is read as vetted programming unless the page itself says otherwise
Supplies framing that asks attendees to support these independently-run events, rather than presenting them as programme
States that a list published without that framing is worse than publishing no list at all
Notes that an open list with no gate is a worse trade than a vetted application despite costing less, because it hands the organizer an endorsement never examined
Requires an explicit non-endorsement line on the page itself
Names who decides, or states explicitly that no gate is being run
Requires the criteria to exist in writing before the first submission arrives if any gate is run
Names apparent endorsement as an exposure the page creates and routes it to counsel
States no monetary figure and names no legal instrument
Presents the page and the posture for validation before publication, noting that publication is the point of no return

evals.prompt: Cobalt Registry bought our "Signature Side Event" package at Ferrolink Conf for 18,000 EUR. It was on the rate card and they signed in January. They want to run a 150-person evening event on our Thursday, call it "Cobalt Night @ Ferrolink", use our wordmark and our brand colour on their invite, and have it appear in our event app. We are an incorporated non-profit and we own the marks ourselves. Our closing keynote is Friday 16:00. They are asking me to just send them the logo files. What do I send back?
evals.expected_output: A response applying the same criteria and approval decision as any unpaid satellite, plus a deliberately scoped name licence - named grantee, named marks, one purpose, a stated end date, materials reviewed before printing - and a withdrawal right kept separate from breach.
expectations: Applies the same criteria set and approval decision to the paid slot as to any unpaid satellite
Recommends a licensed co-branding grant for this case rather than the default non-affiliation wording
Gives the reason: the organizer wants this event read as connected, which is what breaks the usual case against granting a licence
Names Cobalt Registry as the grantee of the licence
Names the specific marks covered rather than gesturing at "branding" or "our assets"
Binds the grant to one stated purpose
Gives the grant a stated end date, or states that it expires automatically rather than continuing silently into future editions
Requires materials be shown to the organizer before they are printed
Keeps a withdrawal right separate from any breach of the criteria, on reputational grounds
States what withdrawal means in practice, including that materials already printed are the sponsor's problem
Imposes adoption of a code of conduct and a named contact as a condition
Deconflicts the Thursday evening slot against the published grid's own protected hours

evals.prompt: Pinefield Systems Day is a 250-person community conference we run in Utrecht. Five or six user groups and a couple of companies usually run something during our two days. The trouble is Joris. He is the only organizer with time to handle this, and he also runs the local JS meetup with half the people who would be applying. He drinks with them every second Thursday. Last year he approved everything, including one thing that turned out to be a recruiting pitch. Our comms volunteer Anouk is on site all week and happy to keep a page updated. What process should we set up?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation for an open self-registration listing rather than a vetting gate, keyed explicitly to Joris being unable to refuse without it being personal, with a maintained shared calendar justified by Anouk plus the number of satellites, and the naming and liability work still done.
expectations: Recommends an open self-registration listing over a vetted application process, and ties that choice to Joris being unable to refuse a request without it being personal
States that a gate that never says no is a worse arrangement than an open list carrying a non-endorsement line
Does not propose a review committee, a scoring rubric or extra reviewers as the fix for Joris
Requires a non-endorsement line on the listing
Uses support framing rather than presenting the listed events as programme
Recommends a shared public calendar only because both a named maintainer (Anouk) and enough satellites exist, not because either alone is satisfied
Still sets a naming rung and supplies the exact sentence satellite organizers must carry
Still names the liability exposure categories and routes each one
States that the liability position is deliberately not ranked against effort or value
Publishes the posture rather than leaving it unstated
Records the posture and its reason so the next edition starts from a decided rule rather than an argument

evals.prompt: Quick one. We listed "The Foundry Sessions" on our fringe page at Ashgrove Tech Week. It is not our event, a local co-working space runs it, and it is an open bar. If someone falls down their stairs drunk on the Thursday night, are we on the hook? Do we need them to sign something, and how much public liability cover should we be asking them to carry? We are in Ireland if that matters.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to answer the liability question, replaced by the named exposure categories with each one routed - to counsel, to the mark holder, to whoever holds privacy obligations - with no figure, no instrument name and no jurisdiction-specific rule stated.
expectations: Declines to state whether the organizer is liable
States no monetary figure for insurance cover or for anything else
Names no legal instrument as the answer
States no Irish or other jurisdiction-specific rule, threshold or statute
States explicitly that the specific rule is jurisdiction-specific
Names the exposure categories at stake instead of answering the question asked
Routes what happens to a person at a third party's venue to counsel
Routes alcohol served by somebody else to counsel
Names apparent endorsement created by listing the event as a distinct exposure
Names personal data collected by the satellite organizer and routes it to whoever holds the organization's privacy obligations
States that the liability position is deliberately not ranked
Offers to carry a chosen category as a scored risk-register row, separately from any disclaimer wording

evals.prompt: Got an email from Tilda, who runs Rustfest Baltic. She wants us to put each other in our newsletters and share a discount code, 15% each way. She also mentions that while she is in town for our event (Kaunas, October 8-10) she would like to run a half-day Rust workshop on the 9th at a co-working space ten minutes from our venue, free entry, and asks whether we would list it and whether she can say "in partnership with Baltcon". How should I handle this?
evals.expected_output: An answer that splits the reciprocal promotion swap from the workshop request, handles the swap as a peer exchange with no hosting or approval involved, and puts only the 9 October workshop through the satellite approval decision including its naming rung.
expectations: Separates the reciprocal newsletter-and-discount swap from the workshop request and handles them differently
States that the promotion swap involves no hosting and no approval by either side, and routes it away from the satellite approval machinery
Treats the 9 October workshop as a satellite requiring its own approval decision
Refuses "in partnership with Baltcon", or requires a deliberate decision on it rather than granting it as a by-product of the promotion swap
Sets a naming rung for the workshop and supplies the exact sentence it must carry
Checks the workshop's timing against the published grid's protected hours
Imposes code-of-conduct adoption and a named on-the-day contact on the workshop only
Asks Tilda to separate exactly what she is requesting: a listing, a mention, permission to use the name, floor space, or nothing
States no monetary figure and names no legal instrument
Records the decision and the criterion behind it
Presents the answer for validation before anything is published or sent

evals.prompt: Two things. First, here is our side-event application form for Halcyon Summit, 14 fields: org name, org logo upload, org website, contact email, VAT number, event name, event description (min 200 words), format, headcount, ticketed yes/no, venue, start and end time, "why your event is a good fit" (min 150 words), social handles. Second, here is the refusal I drafted for a company whose Wednesday product demo runs straight through our opening keynote: "Hi Marek, we love what you're building and would really like to support it, but we're a bit worried about the timing and how it might look to some of our sponsors, so maybe let's see how the schedule shapes up and circle back closer to the date?" Tighten both up.
evals.expected_output: A trimmed form carrying only fields a criterion consumes plus the missing ones (named human reachable during the event, intended name and every place the marks appear, the separated ask, accessibility and alcohol), and a rewritten refusal that names the criterion, states the decision, offers the one remaining option and stops.
expectations: Cuts fields no criterion consumes and names which ones go, such as the VAT number, the logo upload, the social handles or the long free-text essays
States that each added field costs submissions, and that what is lost is how many satellites the organizer learns about at all
Keeps a named human plus a way to reach them during the event, and rejects a brand or shared alias in that field
Adds what the applicant intends to call the event and every place the event's name or logo would appear
Adds what the applicant is actually asking for, separated into listing, mention, permission to use the name, floor space, or nothing
Adds one-line accessibility and alcohol answers
Rewrites the refusal to name the criterion that decided it, the clash with the protected opening keynote
Rewrites it to state the decision plainly, with no deferral and no "circle back"
Offers the one thing still available, moving clear of the protected window to be eligible for listing, and then stops
Removes the softening, the sponsor-optics explanation and the open-endedness from the refusal
States that the criteria are published while individual decisions and refusals are not
Keeps the refusal in the internal decision record alongside approvals
